parity.reason: 3/3 after the hyphen vocabulary fix (2026-09-19): the outcome name 'Heart-failure hospitalization' parsed to NO canonical component, so the target-endpoint selector could not see AFFIRM-AHF's registry row #6 'HF Hospitalisations — number of participants with at least one HF hospitalisation up to 52 weeks' (COUNT_OF_PARTICIPANTS; time to first event; HR 0.73 [0.59, 0.92]; 142/558 vs 178/550): a first-event participant count that IS the declared estimand, now pooled as an EXACT_TARGET. AFFIRM-AHF's recurrent-event measure (#2, 'analysed as recurrent event', RR 0.74) stays refused as a recurrent-event estimand. HEART-FID stays refused: CT.gov labels its heart-failure hospitalizations COUNT_OF_PARTICIPANTS (297/1532 vs 332/1533) while the title counts hospitalizations and the publication says "297 hospitalizations" = RECURRENT EVENTS -- typed UNIT_CONFLICT_EVENTS_VS_PARTICIPANTS, not reconstructed. FAIR-HF = no extractable data; EFFECT-HF = open-label (design-excluded). CONFIRM-HF recovered.

previous.reason: 2/3. Gap = HEART-FID + AFFIRM-AHF, refused on estimand: CT.gov labels HEART-FID heart-failure hospitalizations as COUNT_OF_PARTICIPANTS (297/1532 vs 332/1533) but the publication says "297 hospitalizations" = RECURRENT EVENTS, not patients — pooling the CT.gov count as a binary would produce a wrong number, so the recurrent-event guard refuses it. FAIR-HF = no extractable data; EFFECT-HF = open-label (design-excluded). CONFIRM-HF recovered.

hash_inputs.protocol_sha: registration/build anchor Git commit (SHA-1, not a SHA-256 or prospective-registration claim)

hash_inputs.retrieval_ledger_sha256: canonical entire retrieval_ledger.json (including any raw-index digest)
hash_inputs.held_documents: SHA-256 of exact file bytes at each bundle-relative ref; all topic ft_*.txt/aact_*.json plus referenced held documents and source-manifest PDF/text pairs
